page_title: Drop your footage. Get back a finished edit.

sources.entry: DoneCut - Upload raw footage and an AI editor returns a finished YouTube video or Shorts with captions, motion graphics and music. #paid

summary.name: DoneCut
summary.one_liner: DoneCut is a paid service where you upload raw video footage and an AI editor returns a finished YouTube video or Shorts-style edit, paying half up front and the rest after approval.
keywords: upload raw footage get edited video
use_cases: Cutting mistakes, pauses and dead air from a YouTube talking-head video
Turning a podcast episode into vertical shorts
Making captioned Shorts, Reels or TikToks from raw clips
Editing customer testimonials or product promos
Cutting travel or vlog clips to a music track
summary.what_it_does: DoneCut takes uploaded raw video files (up to 60 minutes of footage for a YouTube edit) and prices the job based on footage length. The page says an AI editor working with professional editing tools cuts the footage, times captions, builds graphics and mixes sound, then checks its work against the user's notes. Customers pay a 50% deposit to start, receive a watermarked preview with up to two rounds of changes, and pay the balance to unlock the clean full-quality file. Pricing is listed as $49 for up to 10 minutes of YouTube footage and $29 per short, with extra footage at $3 per minute.
notable: Price shown instantly after upload, before paying
Half-payment deposit with watermarked preview; balance paid only on approval
Saves logo, brand colors and caption style to match a channel's look over time
Footage deleted 30 days after delivery; not used to train AI
caveats: Paid service: YouTube edits from $49, Shorts from $29
Two rounds of changes included; further changes not described
Turnaround figures are from the company's own test orders and sample edits, not guaranteed
